maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0130-004

Asset: WELL-0130 (NE-07 Well 130, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 26 Apr 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 450 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0130-0025 on 2023-04-06 Report written: 26 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0130-0025 showed the wellhead at 20.9 °C with the air at 16.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0130-004 (WS-06).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0130-008

Asset: WELL-0130 (NE-07 Well 130, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 13 Mar 2024 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 943 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0130-0064 on 2024-02-01 Report written: 13 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0130-0064 showed the wellhead at 10.9 °C with the air at 11.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0130-012

Asset: WELL-0130 (NE-07 Well 130, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 30 Nov 2024 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 16 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0130-0107 on 2024-11-28 Report written: 01 Dec 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0130-0107 at 14:45 on 2024-11-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.5% of the pad area, estimated 3.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 285 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 228 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0130-012 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.5% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
